content:
Apple today released a major update for Final Cut Camera, the professional video app Apple first launched for iPhone in 2024. This update introduces a brand-new design and adds support for the variable aperture on the iPhone 18 Pro.

If you haven't heard of it, Apple touts Final Cut Camera as a tool that lets you "record professional video with complete control and connect to Final Cut Pro for iPad to capture multiple angles in a single take with live multicam." Apple announced the app in May 2024 and released it a month later.

Final Cut Camera version 2.4 starts rolling out today and brings several key changes. First, it introduces a brand-new, more personalized design that makes it easier to access different settings.

This update also adds support for the variable aperture on the iPhone 18 Pro, with an aperture range from f/1.48 to f/4, and offers shutter priority, aperture priority, and manual modes. It also supports Cinematic mode on the iPhone 18 Pro, including video shot in ProRes and Apple Log.

You can download Final Cut Camera from the App Store. The new version starts rolling out from today. The app requires a subscription to Apple Creator Studio, at US$12.99 per month or US$129 per year.
